Exploratory analysis of the in-scope cohort built by the dbt model
`fct_results_reporting`. Input: the export produced by `02_export_for_r.sql`.
Figures are written to `figures/`.

## 0. Setup

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(survival)
library(survminer)

snapshot_date <- as.Date("2026-10-11")   # same as the dbt var snapshot_date
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

trials <- read_csv("../../data/results_reporting_.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Conservation check against dbt: total trials and in-scope trials.
nrow(trials)
sum(trials$in_scope)

cohort <- trials |> filter(in_scope)
```

## 1. Cohort funnel

How the 11,211 registered trials narrow down to the trials that had to report
results. Each excluded trial is counted once, at the first rule it fails.

```{r}
funnel <- trials |>
  count(exclusion_reason) |>
  mutate(exclusion_reason = coalesce(exclusion_reason, "6_in_scope")) |>
  arrange(exclusion_reason) |>
  mutate(remaining_before_step = nrow(trials) - lag(cumsum(n), default = 0))
funnel

ggplot(funnel, aes(x = n, y = reorder(exclusion_reason, desc(exclusion_reason)))) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey60") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Trials", y = NULL,
       title = "Cohort selection: first failed rule per trial") +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("figures/01_funnel.png", width = 7, height = 3.5, dpi = 300)
```

## 2. On-time rate by sponsor, with 95% confidence intervals

On-time rate = ON_TIME / trials whose outcome is known, i.e. trials still within
a requested extension (EXTENSION_REQUESTED) are left out of the denominator,
as in the dbt model.

The small sponsor classes (NIH, NETWORK, OTHER_GOV) are pooled as
"GOV_NETWORK". Confidence intervals are exact (Clopper-Pearson).

```{r}
cohort <- cohort |>
  mutate(sponsor_group = case_when(
    lead_sponsor_class %in% c("INDUSTRY", "OTHER") ~ lead_sponsor_class,
    TRUE ~ "GOV_NETWORK"
  ))

rates <- cohort |>
  filter(reporting_status != "EXTENSION_REQUESTED") |>
  group_by(sponsor_group) |>
  summarise(on_time = sum(reporting_status == "ON_TIME"),
            decided = n(),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    rate  = on_time / decided,
    ci_lb = mapply(function(x, n) binom.test(x, n)$conf.int[1], on_time, decided),
    ci_ub = mapply(function(x, n) binom.test(x, n)$conf.int[2], on_time, decided)
  )
rates
```

The interval for GOV_NETWORK is wide because the group is small.

## 3. Industry vs other sponsors: two-proportion test

```{r}
two <- rates |> filter(sponsor_group %in% c("INDUSTRY", "OTHER"))
two
prop.test(x = two$on_time, n = two$decided)
```

## 3b. Sensitivity analysis: does the extension rule drive the sponsor difference?

Two checks: (1) whether extension requests are more common among industry
trials, and (2) the sponsor comparison repeated with a strict 12-month deadline
for every trial, i.e. without the 36-month allowance for extensions.

```{r}
# (1) Share of trials with an extension request, by sponsor group
ext <- cohort |>
  group_by(sponsor_group) |>
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    n_ext    = sum(extension_requested),
    ext_rate = mean(extension_requested),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ext

ext_two <- ext |> filter(sponsor_group %in% c("INDUSTRY", "OTHER"))
prop.test(x = ext_two$n_ext, n = ext_two$n)
```

```{r}
# (2) Strict definition: results submitted within 365 days of primary
# completion. Trials without a submission count as not on time.
cohort <- cohort |>
  mutate(
    strict_on_time = coalesce(
      results_first_submitted_date <= primary_completion_date + 365,
      FALSE
    )
  )

# All trials are in the denominator, including EXTENSION_REQUESTED: the
# 12-month deadline has passed for every in-scope trial, so the outcome is known.
strict <- cohort |>
  filter(sponsor_group %in% c("INDUSTRY", "OTHER")) |>
  group_by(sponsor_group) |>
  summarise(
    on_time = sum(strict_on_time),
    n       = n(),
    rate    = on_time / n,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
strict

prop.test(x = strict$on_time, n = strict$n)
```

## 4. Time to results submission (Kaplan–Meier)

The binary on-time rate ignores timing: a trial that reports on day 366 counts
the same as one that never reports. A time-to-event analysis keeps it.

- Time origin: primary completion date.
- Event: results first submitted.
- Censoring: trials with no submission yet are censored at the snapshot date.
- Trials with results submitted before primary completion (a registry anomaly,
  flagged by a dbt warning test) are given time 0.

```{r}
km_data <- cohort |>
  mutate(
    event = as.integer(!is.na(results_first_submitted_date)),
    end_date = coalesce(results_first_submitted_date, snapshot_date),
    time_days = pmax(as.numeric(end_date - primary_completion_date), 0),
    time_months = time_days / 30.4375
  )

# Every in-scope trial has passed its 12-month deadline, so no trial is
# censored before 12 months.
summary(km_data$time_months[km_data$event == 0])
```

```{r}
km_two <- km_data |> filter(sponsor_group %in% c("INDUSTRY", "OTHER"))
km_fit <- survfit(Surv(time_months, event) ~ sponsor_group, data = km_two)

# Log-rank test
survdiff(Surv(time_months, event) ~ sponsor_group, data = km_two)

# Share not yet submitted at 12, 24 and 36 months
summary(km_fit, times = c(12, 24, 36))
```

1 − S(12) is close to, but not the same as, the on-time rate in section 2:
the on-time rate uses the legal deadline (36 months for trials with an
extension request), whereas the Kaplan–Meier estimate at 12 months does not.

```{r}
# fun = "event" plots the cumulative share with results submitted (1 - S).
p <- ggsurvplot(
  km_fit, data = km_two,
  fun = "event", conf.int = TRUE, risk.table = TRUE,
  xlim = c(0, 60), break.time.by = 12,
  xlab = "Months since primary completion",
  ylab = "Share with results submitted",
  legend.title = "Lead sponsor", legend.labs = c("Industry", "Other (mainly academic)"),
  pval = TRUE, ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)
p$plot <- p$plot + geom_vline(xintercept = 12, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40")
p
png("figures/02_km_by_sponsor.png", width = 7, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
print(p)
dev.off()
```

## 5. Limitations and next steps

- The cohort requires a reported FDA-regulation flag. Flags are mostly missing
  before ~2020 and the missingness is unlikely to be random, so compliance is
  probably overestimated.
- Associations only. Next: Cox model adjusting for phase, enrollment and
  completion year; the Kaplan–Meier curves cross, so the proportional-hazards
  assumption has to be checked.
- Extensions are modelled with a single 36-month deadline (simplification).
